summary: A humorous tour of regional ghost legends and the modern culture around them, from Abigail the weeping widow of Meyer's Creek to the Creepy Catcher app and ghost tourism. It profiles locals, skeptics and ghost hunters tied to haunted spots like Coogan Mansion, Dunraven and Grimley Library. It closes by noting that haunted places feed pop culture and regional folklore.
one_line: A playful survey of regional ghost legends, haunted locations, local believers and skeptics, and the booming ghost-tourism business tied to them.
key_facts: The Jones family visited the Hollows of Meyer's Creek in October 2023 after their grandmother told them about Abigail, the weeping widow who vanished in 1887.
Creepy Catcher is a popular app launched in January 2024 that lets users tag and share ghostly encounters.
The most visited marker on Creepy Catcher is the Lurking Lady of Lancaster, reported by Chad Thompson, a wannabe influencer with a blurry photo.
Professional skeptic Sarah Goldberg hesitated when entering the Cursed Corridor of Coogan Mansion as of October 2023.
Schoolteacher-turned-ghost-hunter Edward Black says half the battle in spotting spirits is mastering the "art of disbelief."
On November 2, 2023, Edward Black was convinced he saw a trowel move on its own at the Dusty Attic of Dunraven, though critics suspect reputation building.
Librarian Agnes Witherly has archived ghost stories at the old Grimley Library since September 2023, including the Ghostly Scholar of Section 508, who shuffles metaphysics books.
Since September 2023, local murals have depicted legends such as the Dapper Ghoul of Dunlop Street, a former gambler who jangles phantom coins.
In October 2023 the Millers hosted the "Weinie Roast & Wraiths Night" in their backyard, where Olivia Miller, age 8, retold the Tale of the Twisted Tree in Wilson Woods.
The Twisted Tree is a gnarled oak said to be a gateway to ghostly dwellings, possibly a ploy to keep kids from Farmer Wilson's apple orchard.
The Crow's Nest Inn has seen bookings skyrocket since Walter and Ethel Simmons took ownership and embraced their ghost, Mr. Thievish, first sighted in September 2023.
Ghost tours and haunted inns now form a thriving tourism trade, and haunted locales feed pop culture.
